xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheAuthority: Assistant Commissioner of Customs Export, ACC, Mumbai Customs Zone III
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: The Assistant Commissioner of Customs (Export), ACC, Mumbai Customs Zone III, has passed a Denovo Adjudication Order-in-Original passed in the case of Gufic Lifesciences Private Limited (currently merged with Gufic Biosciences Limited), imposing a penalty of ₹25,000 under Section 117 of the Customs Act, 1962 for alleged differential duty drawback claim. Of this amount, ₹2,000 has already been paid, and the remaining balance is recoverable. The Company is in the process of filing an appeal against the order.

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: There is no material impact on financials, operations or other activities of the Company.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: Appeal is filed before the Hon’ble Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), National Faceless Appeal Centre, Delhi, on April 14, 2025, against the Assessment Order dated March 18, 2025, passed under Section 143(3) read with Section 144B of the Income Tax Act, 1961, by the Income Tax Department for Assessment Year 2023–24. The appeal challenges the disallowance of certain deductions claimed by the Company, which were disallowed without affording the Company an adequate opportunity for explanation. The amount of demand is Rs. 11,88,88,580/-. The appeal of the Company is treated as partly-allowed.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Income Tax Department has filed an appeal before the Hon’ble Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) against the relief granted to the Company. The Company has filed a cross-objection before ITAT in respect of the disallowances contested. The matter is pending for hearing.
